deployments: deploy:MaliciousFeeController exposing fetchDynamicFeeForSwapIn/Out returning abi.encode(uint256(0), true)
deploy:FluidDexV2D3 (or D4) instance with controller = MaliciousFeeController
addr:<existing FluidDexV2D3 pool with fetchDynamicFee flag enabled>

assertions: dexVariables2 BITS_DEX_V2_VARIABLES2_FETCH_DYNAMIC_FEE_FLAG == 1 (controller-driven dynamic fee enabled)
dexKey.controller is set to MaliciousFeeController address
Pool has non-zero active liquidity in current tick range
Honest LP has supplied liquidity in [tickLower, tickUpper] expecting LP fees from swap volume
setup_calls: Admin sets dexKey.controller = MaliciousFeeController and flips fetchDynamicFee flag ON
LP calls deposit() to provide liquidity expecting fee accrual
Swappers route trades through the pool

post_vuln_state.custom_assertion: feeGrowthGlobal0X102 and feeGrowthGlobal1X102 remain unchanged after swap volume; LP withdraw returns zero feeAccruedToken0/1 despite non-trivial swap volume across the position's tick range

attack_steps: Controller deploys MaliciousFeeController whose fetchDynamicFeeForSwapIn() / fetchDynamicFeeForSwapOut() always return abi.encode(uint256(0), true) — exactly 64 bytes, success=true.
At swapModuleInternals.sol L77-L83: low-level call succeeds, returnData_.length == 64. abi.decode yields fetchedDynamicFee_=0 and overrideDynamicFee_=true.
Bound check at L80 'if (fetchedDynamicFee_ > X16) overrideDynamicFee_ = false' does NOT trigger because 0 <= X16. The override remains active.
Branch at L86 takes overrideDynamicFee_ == true: v_.isConstantLpFee = true; v_.constantLpFee = 0.
In the swap loop at L156-L159: 'if (stepAmountOutRaw_ > 0 && v_.constantLpFee > 0) stepLpFeeRaw_ = ...' — short-circuits because constantLpFee == 0. stepLpFeeRaw_ stays 0.

feeGrowthGlobal{0,1}X102 update at L207-L211: 'feeGrowthGlobal{0,1}X102 += ((stepLpFeeRaw_ * exchangePrice) / EXCHANGE_PRICES_PRECISION) << 102 / activeLiquidity_' adds ZERO because stepLpFeeRaw_ == 0.

Across thousands of swaps over hours/days, LPs in the active tick range receive ZERO LP fees while the controller's malicious returnvalue silently zeroes every swap's fee — even from swappers who never interacted with the controller.

Symmetric DoS-griefing variant: returning (X16, true) — exactly 65535 (= 6.5535%) — passes the L80 bound check (only > X16 is rejected, equality accepted) and combined with high protocolCutFee inflates output-side fee deduction to make swaps revert in slippage checks for honest users.
preconditions: DEX pool has FETCH_DYNAMIC_FEE_FLAG == 1 (set by admin during initialization or via update)
dexKey.controller is mutable per pool (set at admin module level)
The msg.sender of the swap is NOT the controller (the controller-self path skips the fetch)
hypotheses.rationale: Bound check is one-sided (only upper bound > X16 rejected). Zero LP fee is permitted as a 'valid' override return, violating the implicit invariant that an LP earns fees proportional to (volume * fee_rate) when they hold liquidity in an active range. KG-similar incidents: 2023-04 Allbridge (oracle-controlled fee), 2023-07 ArcadiaFi (price-feed override). Fluid Dex specifically inherits this surface from dynamic-fee design choice. Even if controller is admin-trusted, the *silent per-swap* nature means a single malicious deploy bypasses all governance/timelock event-monitoring expected for protocol fee changes.

verification.evidence: Static reading of swapModuleInternals.sol L70-L96 (swapIn) and L394-L422 (swapOut); _validateLPFee at helpers.sol L696 confirms 0 is also a valid LP fee but the *per-swap* override path bypasses any admin-fee floor enforcement.

deployments: addr:<initialised D4 pool with non-zero reserves>

assertions: Pool is initialized (sqrtPriceX96 != 0).
Borrower is whitelisted: _whitelistedUsers[4][borrower] == 1.
Borrower controls position salt to keccak fresh positions per call.
setup_calls: Pool already has supply liquidity in adjacent tick ranges (from honest LPs in D3).

post_vuln_state.custom_assertion: After N calls to borrow() with minimal amount0/amount1, sum_i(positionData_.liquidity_i) > sum_i(LA.getLiquidityForAmounts(... amount0_i, amount1_i)). The aggregated liquidity over many tiny borrows exceeds what the underlying token reserves justify, allowing the attacker to over-borrow against under-reserved positions.

attack_steps: Compute the smallest non-zero borrow amounts that survive _verifyAdjustedAmountLimits and _verifyReserveAndDebtLimits.

Call borrow() with isSmartCollateral=false (D4 path). Internal _addLiquidity at L40-L42 applies 'liquidityIncreaseRaw_ = ((liquidityIncreaseRaw_ * (R+1)) / R) + 1' — strictly INFLATES liquidity beyond what user's amount0/amount1 justify.
_addLiquidity then re-derives reserves with getAmountsForLiquidity using the inflated liquidity (L46-L51). Returned amount0Raw_ / amount1Raw_ are larger than the user's input desired amounts.
Caller (d4 borrow) takes these inflated reserves and converts them to debt via _getDebtAmountsFromReserves — debt is also inflated.

Critical dust-effect: the '+ 1' constant added unconditionally accrues across each call. After K borrow() iterations on tiny positions (different positionSalt each), accumulated 'free liquidity' = K added with bounded extra reserves — pool's recorded liquidity is greater than the sum of token reserves it actually backs.
Subsequent legitimate liquidations / withdrawals draw down reserves at the inflated debt scale; the protocol becomes under-collateralized.
Attacker repeats borrow + immediate payback (or borrow + withdraw of position) ratcheting up share of pool liquidity per token deposited.
preconditions: Borrower is whitelisted for D4 (admin gate).
Pool min/max amount limits are gameable — attacker can find amount0/amount1 that yield liquidityIncreaseRaw_ > 0 but where the +1 dust is significant relative to position size.
hypotheses.rationale: The unconditional '+ 1' on rounded-up liquidity is dust per call but compounds across many positions. Distinct from the documented 'protocol-on-winning-side' direction because it is applied to LIQUIDITY (a state quantity tracked across positions) rather than to a transient amount. The recomputed amounts/debt scale linearly with this inflated liquidity, breaking the invariant that sum(position liquidity) ≈ implied liquidity from total reserves.

verification.evidence: Static reading of userModuleInternals.sol L34-L52 (smart-debt branch); compare D3 path which rounds DOWN with no +1 added. The asymmetry in rounding direction means smart-debt positions claim MORE liquidity per token than smart-collateral positions, which would only be safe if separately accounted — but _addLiquidity is shared.

deployments: addr:<FluidDexV2 D3 or D4 pool with feeVersion == 1 (dynamic fee enabled)>

assertions: Pool feeVersion == 1 (dynamic fee path active)
Pool has non-zero netPriceImpact and non-zero decayTimeRemaining stored from prior heavy-volume period
No swaps occur for at least 32768 seconds (~9.1 hours) — covering one or more 15-bit timestamp wraps
setup_calls: Phase 1: attacker performs heavy swap volume that pushes |finalNetPriceImpact_| close to maxFee/divisionFactor cap, sets DECAY_TIME_REMAINING to 4095s.
Phase 2: wait for 32768 + Δ seconds where Δ is small (e.g. 60s) so newLastUpdateTimestamp_ % X15 ≈ original lastUpdateTimestamp_ + Δ.
Phase 3: attacker performs the *first* swap of the new wrap window.

post_vuln_state.custom_assertion: After the wrap-around swap, dexVariables2 still encodes a non-zero ABSOLUTE_NET_PRICE_IMPACT, even though wall-clock decayTimeRemaining + Δ has elapsed since the last update — i.e. the decay is at least 32768 seconds OVERDUE relative to its own logic.

attack_steps: L168 stores `newLastUpdateTimestamp_ = block.timestamp & X15` — only the low 15 bits of block.timestamp.

L171-L181: If newLastUpdateTimestamp_ < lastUpdateTimestamp_, code adds X15+1 (i.e. 32768s) and computes `timeElapsed_ = X15 + 1 + new - last`. If the wrap is exactly one cycle the math is correct, but if MULTIPLE wraps occurred (≥2 × 32768s = 18.2h+), timeElapsed_ underestimates by k×32768 seconds.

L173-L177 comments acknowledge: 'More time than this might have passed, but we assume the minimum'. The author intentionally uses the minimum timeElapsed_, but compares it against decayTimeRemaining_ which is bounded by X12 = 4095s.

Branch at L186 `if (timeElapsed_ < decayTimeRemaining_)` is reached when wrapped-modulo elapsed appears small. The decay update L190 `netPriceImpact_ * (decayTimeRemaining_ - timeElapsed_) / decayTimeRemaining_` preserves a fraction of the price-impact memory that should have decayed to zero many hours ago.

Attacker exploits stale netPriceImpact_ to either (a) get systematically lower fees on subsequent swaps (if pool's own feeKink is favorable) or (b) trigger artificial maxFee branches on a competing user's swap (DoS griefing).

Specifically, the netPriceImpact_ feeds into L209 `d_.zeroPriceImpactPriceX96` which directly sets the swap-time fee curve. A stale POSITIVE netPriceImpact_ on a pool where actual price has already mean-reverted means the fee model over-charges or under-charges every subsequent swap until a 'real' large swap re-syncs it.
preconditions: Pool uses feeVersion 1 (dynamic fee). Set by controller via _updateFeeVersion1.
decayTimeRemaining_ is at most X12 = 4095s, so any pool inactivity > ~68min already exceeds the decay window — yet the bug only triggers ONCE per wrap window.
Low-volume pools (small altcoin pairs) most exposed: may have multiple 9-hour gaps without organic swaps.
hypotheses.rationale: The 'assume minimum elapsed' strategy is correct *only* if the 15-bit timestamp can never wrap more than once between calls. In a low-volume pool this assumption fails. The author's comment ('More time than this might have passed, but we assume the minimum') confirms the sub-optimal handling, but the consequence — a fee curve frozen with stale net price impact — is silent and persistent. A 15-bit timestamp window (32768s) is shorter than common DEX inactivity windows for small pairs, especially on L2s during low-activity hours.

verification.evidence: Static reading of helpers.sol L161-L210; bit-position check (LAST_UPDATE_TIMESTAMP=229 width 15, DECAY_TIME_REMAINING=244 width 12) confirmed in dexV2D3D4CommonSlotsLink.sol L56-L57. The MAX decayTimeRemaining 4095s is documented and matches X12.
